chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the loaned item (ariyyah); if a person borrows it and it perishes or is stolen, he said: 'If he is trustworthy (amin), there is no compensation (ghurm) upon him.'

key_terms.الْعَارِيَّةِ: A loaned item given for use without rent

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a borrowed item is stolen or lost?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that liability for a borrowed item (ariyyah) is contingent upon negligence; if the borrower is 'amin' (trustworthy and not at fault), they are exempt from compensation (ghurm) even if the item is lost or stolen. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that bailment is generally gratuitous and liability arises only from specific fault or breach of condition, distinguishing it from rental contracts.
